subject: physics_2
question_text: What did the experiments of Faraday and Henry show?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: a galvanometer joined to a coil deflects when a magnet moves relative to the coil, or when the current in a neighbouring coil changes; the deflection lasts only while the change lasts, so the common cause is a changing magnetic flux.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The observation
lines: When a magnet is moved towards a coil or
away from it, the galvanometer joined to
the coil shows a deflection. The same
happens when the current in a nearby coil
The deflection lasts only while the motion
or the change of current continues.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name both experiments: a moving magnet, and a changing current in a nearby coil.
steps.why: The two experiments differ in the cause — motion in one, a changing current in the other — but both change the magnetic flux through the coil. Showing both is what points to flux as the common cause.
common_mistakes: Saying a magnet near the coil induces a current. A stationary magnet induces nothing; something must change.
Naming only the moving-magnet experiment. Henry's changing-current experiment carries the same point.

recall.must_convey: That relative motion between a magnet and a coil, or a changing current in a nearby coil, gives a deflection only while the change continues.
accept: changing current in a nearby coil

steps.memory_tip: Two set-ups, one result: move the magnet, or change the current next door. The needle moves only while something is changing.

steps.label: What the experiments show
lines: So the experiments show: whenever the
magnetic flux linked with a coil changes,
an emf is induced in the coil. This is

lines.text: A changing magnetic flux induces an emf

steps.margin_note: Second mark. The one-line conclusion in terms of flux is what the examiner reads for.
steps.why: Motion and a changing current look different, but both change the flux through the coil. Stating the conclusion in terms of flux covers both experiments in one law.
common_mistakes: Stopping at the observations. The question asks what the experiments SHOW, so the flux conclusion must be written.

recall.must_convey: That a changing magnetic flux through a coil induces an emf in it.
accept: emf is induced when flux changes
reject: the deflection lasts while the motion lasts

steps.memory_tip: The conclusion is one line: change the flux, get an emf.

insider_note: The observation alone is half the answer; the examiner reads for the one-line conclusion that a changing flux induces an emf.
